note: Every capture here is SYNTHETIC. These cases exercise the analyzer; they say nothing about any device. Expected files are worked out by hand (and cross-checked by tests/e02/oracle.py), never produced by the analyzer. Each expected file is a SUBSET of the report: named keys must match exactly, arrays must match in length and element by element.

cases.title: clean capture: full coverage, dropouts known to be zero, absolute verdict without any baseline
five underruns, one per evidence class: source outage, network lateness, CPU deadline miss, output underrun, ambiguous
underrun with no discriminating signals in the capture: undetermined, missing signals named
no underrun counter and no device clock: dropout count is unknown, not zero, and a zero-dropout threshold is not met
coverage hole with events inside it: reported, never interpolated, events unlocated
capture ends before its declared duration: truncation reported, no extrapolation
32-bit wraparound counted exactly; 32-bit and 64-bit resets censored, never a negative rate
wall clock steps forward and back: reported, no fake gap or dropout, real dropout still found
implausible reading rejected, spike kept and flagged, percentiles by nearest rank
device sample clock: drift against monotonic time, 32-bit wrap is not a stall, a real stall is found
out-of-order and duplicate timestamps rejected and counted, never re-ordered
two snapshots: a shared page counted once (PSS), naive RSS double count reported, kernel memory kept apart, peak and headroom
contradictory /proc inputs are reported as findings and nothing is silently corrected
16 KiB pages: statm page counts convert through the explicit page size; absent fields stay absent
comparative claim without a baseline is refused
a synthetic capture cannot serve as the incumbent baseline
a margin of 100% or more is refused rather than clamped
wrong capture schema version is refused at line 1
a sample naming an undeclared series is refused
a non-integer timestamp is refused
a /proc value with the wrong unit is refused, not guessed
unknown subcommand prints usage and exits 2

invariants.text: kB/KiB/page conversions use an explicit page size; a wrong unit is an error
a shared page is counted once (PSS); the naive RSS overstatement is reported
kernel buffers and driver residual are accounted separately from process RSS
peak and steady memory both reported; headroom judged only against a reserve declared in the input
a field the kernel does not provide stays absent, never zero
coverage and sample denominators are exact integers
gaps are coverage holes; events inside them are unlocated, never spread
a capture that ends early reports what is missing and does not extrapolate
a falling monotonic counter is a reset, never a negative rate
a physically possible 32-bit wraparound is counted exactly
a wall-clock step creates no gap and no dropout
the device sample clock is related to monotonic time by drift, not mixed with it
source outage, network lateness, CPU deadline miss and output underrun are told apart by their own signals
without the discriminating signal the cause is undetermined and the missing signal is named
no dropout signal in the capture means unknown, never zero
implausible readings are excluded and counted; spikes are kept and flagged
absolute results and declared-threshold verdicts work with no comparison baseline
a comparative claim without a measured baseline is refused, by type
malformed or ambiguous input is rejected with a typed, bounded, line-numbered error

invariants.inapplicable: The analyzer is a pure batch function over a file: it has no long-running work to cancel and no state to restart from, and it writes its single report only after the whole input has been analyzed, so there is no partial-report state. A killed run produces no output.

No incumbent resource or dropout capture exists in either repository and this task has no authority over a live device. Measuring the incumbent is a separate externally authorised receipt that this analyzer would consume; nothing here claims it.
